subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of the given idiom/phrase from the options:
"Go against the grain"

options.text: To move in the wrong direction

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **To oppose the norm**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Go against the grain"** means to do something contrary to what is generally expected or accepted; it refers to opposing the norm or natural inclination. (आम मान्यता या प्रवृत्ति के खिलाफ जाना) • **Example:** His decision to quit a high-paying job to pursue his passion for painting really goes against the grain. • **"To oppose the norm"** aligns perfectly with the meaning of the idiom "Go against the grain." (आम मान्यता का विरोध करना) • **Example:** Introducing a new work culture in a traditional company might feel like going against the grain. • Hence, the correct meaning of the idiom is **"To oppose the norm."** Therefore, the correct answer is: **To oppose the norm**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **To move in the wrong direction** (गलत दिशा में जाना): Refers to physically or metaphorically heading in an undesired or incorrect way. • **Example:** If you keep ignoring advice, you might move in the wrong direction in life. • **To feel uncomfortable** (असहज महसूस करना): Refers to experiencing unease or awkwardness. • **Example:** He felt uncomfortable when asked about his personal life during the meeting. • **To cut something** (किसी चीज को काटना): Refers to physically dividing or separating something using a sharp tool. • **Example:** She used scissors to cut the ribbon during the ceremony. 3b:T9ef, The correct answer is: **Red tape**.
